text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Retailer Macintosh seeks to take a 50 percent stake in shoe and sporting gear chain Hoogenbosch. (p1)
- PM Wim Kok says chance of European Economic and Monetary Union being postponed is minimal. (p1)
- Kitchenware maker Atag gives no profits forecast because of uncertain situation of German market. (p1)
- Education minister Jo Ritzen calls crisis in European information and communication technology a chance to get ahead of competition. (p1)
- Justice ministry and Holland Casino direction are to intensify control on potential moneylaundering activities. (p1)
- National investment bank NIB puts reserve for general banking risks, which was hidden up to now, into an open fund. (p3)
- Number of Dutch companies that collapsed last year falls 4.1 percent to 5,560 compared to 1995. (p4)
- The Netherlands leads Europe in terms of growth in industrial production in 1996 with 4.4 percent increase. (p6)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Eurocommissioner Hans van den Broek says no to becoming leader of the candidates list for the Christian Democrats Party. (p1)
- Union VHP-Philips worried about Philips Electronics' future, if the company does not give research a leading role.
- Seed company Barenburg of Oosterhout takes majority stake in New Zealand's Agriseeds. (p2)
- Vendex Food group to transform nine Dagmarkt Supermarkets into Via-convenience formula. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Disco party in province of North Holland ends in bloodshed: two dead. (p1)
- Parliament supports justice minister Winnie Sorgdrager's intention to prosecute broadcasters transmitting films containing sex and violence before 9 p.m. (p3)
- Dutch companies operating internationally transfer a growing number of activities abroad, according to accountancy KPMG's research. (p13)
- Dutch cheese exports to France drop six percent in 1996 compared to the year before. (p139)
TROUW
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma thinks parliament should be involved at an earlier stage of the decision making process in large projects. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Bank insurer ING wants Tokyo's financial market to become competitive with London and New York sooner than the 2001 date proposed by Japan's PM Hashimoto.
